season.evidence: Logged ascents Jul 40, Aug 29, Sep 21 (Jun 4, Oct 1, May 1); stored Jul-Sep with August best; web: Mountaineers, SummitPost and WTA reports show mid-summer to early fall, with snow and moat issues earlier.

track.why: 27 Aug 2025 round trip from Pete Lake to the PCT, Vista Lakes area, the notch in the south ridge and the summit (end 59 m from the stored trailhead; summit within 17 m); the report describes the steep loose crux near 6,900 ft where our text places the moat, matching the South Route line. The peak's only other non-ice entry, Southeast Face, is an empty stub on the same face.

otherTracksConsidered.why: 2 Jul 2026 round trip, but the track also wanders west toward the Lemah/Chikamin side (link-up), and early July.
30 Aug 2025 round trip with no elevations; the party says its up-track included fifth-class moves, so the line departs from the standard one.
Part of a multi-day Lemah traverse with Chikamin and Lemah; starts mid-route.

facts.text: Around 6,900 ft the slope is steep loose grit over packed dirt; it is much easier while snow still covers it earlier in summer.
After the notch in the south ridge, take the loose scree gully around the back toward the summit block; heading straight up the face in late August meant solo fifth-class moves.
Crampons and ice axe (early to mid July, when snow still lies in the basin)
From mid-July through early September the upper gullies are very loose and dirty; descending is slower than climbing and rocks released fall on parties below.

season.evidence: No stored season; the peak's logged ascents run mainly Jul-Sep.

notes: Southeast Face looks like a duplicate of the South Route (that route's face is stored as 'Southeast Face / Basin'); consider merging. Summit pin and Peakbagger agree within ~30 m.
